A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 26-page versions of TRACE, including Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval, forecasting, classification and ablation results in Tables 1–6, plus embedding, case-study and runtime results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main experimental tables and the supplementary analyses and runtime measurements in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C retain the same channel identity tokens, channel-biased attention, dual-level contrastive alignment, hard-negative mining and retrieval-augmented prompting procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same curated weather dataset and TimeMMD Health, Energy and Environment subsets for the same retrieval, forecasting and weather-event classification tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in all reported experiments. TimesFM's citation changes from [55] to [33] in Section 4.1 and Appendix D.1, but its evaluated model and results remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The data splits in Table 8, retrieval query counts, metrics, forecasting horizons, model configurations and training procedures in Section 4 and Appendix D are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same component and hyperparameter ablations, embedding visualizations, model-size comparisons, retrieval case studies and efficiency analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use five runs with different random seeds and retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices, including the plus/minus reporting in Table 6.

E6.justification: All result entries and plotted findings match, including the appendices. For example, Table 4 retains TRACE classification accuracy of 85.20% without RAG and 89.76% with RAG; Tables 11–12 retain the same classification and runtime measurements.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem definition, attention formulas, alignment objectives in Appendix C and complexity derivations in Appendix D.9.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about multimodal retrieval, benchmark establishment and standalone and retrieval-augmented performance.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same limitations concerning aligned textual supervision, noisy or missing context and computational overhead.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hyperparameters, hardware, data-generation prompts, fine-tuning instructions and code-access links remain unchanged in Section 4.1 and Appendices B–D.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged. The bibliography shrinks from 59 to 58 entries by consolidating conflicting same-title TimesFM references; the other edits revise metadata for retained works rather than introduce different research.

P1.justification: Limited editorial changes revise bibliography authors, titles, venues, dates and identifiers, including entries for Time-MMD, TS2Vec and PatchTST. Citation numbers and the arXiv version/date stamp change; the main narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Changed reference lengths reflow the bibliography across pages 11–14, moving entries [33] and [50] onto subsequent pages. All 12 numbered tables and 10 figures retain their displays, captions and locations.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves an internal citation inconsistency: v2 cites TimesFM as [33] in Section 2 but uses the conflicting same-title [55] in Section 4.1 and Appendix D.1; v3 consistently uses [33]. This modestly improves citation consistency, partly offset by reduced author or publication detail in some entries, such as PatchTST. The scientific argument, empirical evidence and reproducibility information are unchanged.
